First of all, I know nothing about photography. I need to take several pictures of my fiance and I for my wedding website, but my camera got stolen last month, and now I only have an Iphone. My fiance doesn't want someone else to take pictures, not even a student ( and I found one for free online!). So how can I take my pictures with an Iphone without them looking... horrible?
Hopefully you guys won't hate me for my question...

Hmmm well it'll definitely be pretty hard to do. Honestly getting a student to do them for free would probably be a better bet than doing them yourself with your iphone. I'd try to convince your fiance to go that route if I was you.

But if that REALLY isn't an option then I'd say just try really hard to make sure the photos composition is decent, and you take the photos in a nice area with plenty of light (so that you don't have to use high iso).

Like I said though I'd highly recommend against this route because you won't be able to print the photos very large without them looking kinda crappy, and although a student's quality of work can vary highly (I'm a student and my fellow student photographers work varies from absolutely amazing to complete garbage) it'd probably be a lot better in the end to go this route.

Also think about it this way, technology changes for the better all the time. When you're 80 you might regret that you went with the iphone option considering that iphone photos usually don't look that great even right now. Just imagine how you'll feel about the quality of the photos when you're older and the tech is much much better than it is right now.

Either way though you can probably get decent photos if you put in the effort. Also a word of advice. DONT SKIMP ON THE WEDDING PHOTOGRAPHY. You'll be spending all this money on a dress that'll be worn for one day, food that'll be gone in minutes, and all these other things that won't last (other than in your memory). Your wedding photos will still be around when you and your wife are super old. Therefore it's very important that you pick out a good wedding photographer who knows what they're doing and that you trust. I see people skimp out on this area of the wedding (or even skipping it) all the time, and as a photographer it drives me nuts. One day in the near future they (and hopefully not you) will regret that they didn't pay those big bucks to a wedding photographer who knew what they were doing.

/rant over lol. Sorry for the wall of text. I just wanna make sure you have decent photos to show your grandkids when you're old.
